title: Pakistan | SBP Business Conduct and Fair Treatment of Consumers
tagline: Apply SBP's 2025 BC&FRF at a conventional bank: fair sales, clear disclosure, fair lending and collection, complaints, the Mohtasib and data secrecy.
description:
This quest teaches the conduct and consumer protection rules that apply to conventional banks in Pakistan. It is based on the **State Bank of Pakistan's Business Conduct and Fair Treatment of Consumers Regulatory Framework (BC&FRF)**, issued through BPRD Circular No. 4 of 2025, and on the **Banking Companies Ordinance 1962**: section 33A on fidelity and secrecy, and Part IVA on the **Banking Mohtasib**.

The BC&FRF requires banks to make sure staff are trained, competent and monitored on responsible conduct and fair treatment, to run regular training for employees at all levels, including third-party staff, and to follow an annual training plan with refresher courses and separate programmes for new and existing staff. This quest supports that duty for branch, sales, credit, collections, call-centre, complaints and operations staff and their managers.

In five stages you join the conduct team of a fictional Pakistani bank: the framework and its governance, disclosure and fair sales, lending, collections and inclusion, complaints and the Mohtasib, and finally data secrecy, training and inspection readiness.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own conduct, FTC and complaint policies and procedures; always follow them and the latest SBP instructions.
audience: Branch, account-opening and customer service staff at conventional banks in Pakistan who disclose terms and handle complaints
Sales, relationship and bancassurance staff, including outsourced telesales agents, who sell bank and third-party products
Credit, consumer finance and collections staff, and managers of collection agencies working for banks
Complaint management, call-centre and service quality teams, and the conduct and compliance functions
Senior managers, management committee members and board members who oversee conduct risk
outcomes: Explain the BC&FRF's scope, its outcome-based principles A to H and its six pillars, and who in the bank answers for conduct
Apply SBP's disclosure, KFS, advertising and telemarketing rules, and spot mis-selling and harmful incentives
Lend and collect within the BC&FRF's rules on rates, prepayment, notices, contact and eCIB reporting
Serve persons with disabilities, pensioners and other vulnerable customers with the care the framework requires
Handle complaints within Pillar 5's timelines and explain escalation to SBP's Sunwai portal and the Banking Mohtasib
Protect customer data under Pillar 4 and BCO section 33A, and show the training, reporting and audit evidence SBP expects

quest.name: The Fair Deal Mission
quest.premise: You have just joined Kohsar Bank, a fictional conventional bank headquartered in Islamabad with branches across Pakistan, as its Conduct and Fair Treatment Officer. A retired teacher in Multan says he asked for a fixed deposit and was sold a ten-year insurance plan, and an SBP review is on the way. With Head of Conduct Zara Hashmi, complaints chief Mehwish Anjum, sales head Kamran Sheikh and branch manager Usman Baloch, clear five stages, then face the final boss: the reviewer's exam.

badge.name: Fair Deal Champion
badge.description: Awarded to bankers who can apply SBP's BC&FRF: fair sales, clear disclosure, fair lending and collection, complaint handling, the Mohtasib route and data secrecy.

cast.name: Zara Hashmi
cast.role: Head of Conduct and FTC, Islamabad, your mentor

sessions.title: The BC&FRF: Conduct Risk, FTC Principles and Governance
sessions.summary: Meet SBP's Business Conduct and Fair Treatment of Consumers Regulatory Framework: who it covers, its eight outcome-based principles, its six pillars, and how the board, the management committee, the conduct function and internal audit share responsibility for fair conduct.
objectives: Explain what the BC&FRF is, which institutions it covers and how its two parts and six pillars fit together
Apply the eight FTC outcome-based principles (A to H) to everyday banking decisions
Describe the duties of the board, the management committee, the conduct function and internal audit
Explain the code of conduct, KPI and reward duties that extend to employees and third-party staff

cards.title: Day one at Kohsar Bank
cards.setting: Conduct and FTC department, Kohsar Bank head office, Blue Area, Islamabad. 9:00 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Kohsar Bank, a fictional conventional bank with branches from Gilgit to Gwadar, as its new Conduct and Fair Treatment Officer.
Welcome! I'm Zara Hashmi, Head of Conduct and FTC. Your desk comes with SBP's new framework and, I'm afraid, a pile of complaints.
Mehwish Anjum, complaints unit, Lahore. Top of the pile: a retired teacher in Multan says he asked for a fixed deposit and left with a ten-year insurance plan.
Kamran Sheikh, regional sales head, Karachi. That branch hit 140 percent of its bancassurance target that month. The customer signed every page. Where is the problem?
A signature is no longer the test. SBP now asks whether the customer was treated fairly and ended up with something that suits him.
So who decides what 'fair' means? Me, compliance, the board?
All of us, and the framework says exactly who does what. Stage one is the Charter Room. Learn the rulebook first, then we open the Multan file together.

scenes.heading: One framework
scenes.narration: In October 2025 the State Bank of Pakistan issued the Business Conduct and Fair Treatment of Consumers Regulatory Framework, the BC&FRF, through BPRD Circular No. 4 of 2025. It gathers SBP's conduct and consumer protection rules in one place.

scenes.heading: Who it covers
scenes.narration: It applies to banks, development finance institutions, electronic money institutions and payment system operators and service providers, each only for the business it is allowed to do. For banks, that includes commercial banks, foreign bank branches, microfinance banks and digital banks.

scenes.heading: Conduct risk
scenes.narration: SBP defines conduct risk as customers being exposed to harmful outcomes because of the way a financial institution behaves. The risk sits in culture, strategy, products, processes and the behaviour of staff, including third-party staff.

scenes.heading: Two parts
scenes.narration: Part One sets eight outcome-based principles, lettered A to H, which are binding obligations. Part Two turns them into detailed rules grouped under six pillars.

scenes.heading: Why you are here
scenes.narration: The framework says staff must be trained, competent and monitored on responsible conduct, and that banks must run regular training and awareness sessions for employees at all levels, third-party staff included.

cards.title: The six pillars of Part Two
cards.caption: Part One's principles say what outcome customers should get; the pillars say how the institution delivers it.

items.label: 1. Governance and oversight
items.detail: Board, management committee, code of conduct, KPIs, rewards and internal audit set the culture.

items.label: 2. Disclosure and transparency
items.detail: Clear, accurate information in English and Urdu, Key Fact Statements and honest advertising.

items.label: 3. Fair treatment and conduct
items.detail: Suitability, no unfair practices, fair lending and collection, and support for vulnerable customers.

items.label: 4. Data protection and privacy
items.detail: Lawful, consent-based use of customer data and strict confidentiality from onboarding to closure.

items.label: 5. Dispute resolution
items.detail: Accessible complaint handling with set timelines and information about the second forum.

items.label: 6. Awareness and capacity building
items.detail: A training policy and annual plan for staff, and an awareness policy for customers.

cards.title: Principles A to H in plain words
cards.prompt: Match each FTC principle to what it expects of the bank.

pairs.right: Highest ethical standards; no market manipulation or collusion; no complacency about conduct
Timely, clear, consistent and accurate information that lets customers decide for themselves
Customers are not unfairly disadvantaged or discriminated against when they seek a service
Products fit the customer's needs, affordability, risk appetite and objectives
Charges match the service, compare with other banks and rest on empirical analysis
Data handled lawfully, securely and transparently, with compensation if a breach occurs

cards.question: Kohsar Bank also serves large corporate clients. Which Part One principle does the framework apply only to retail customers?
options: Principle G: lawful, secure and transparent handling of data
Principle B: timely, clear and accurate disclosure
Principle E: products suited to needs, affordability and risk appetite
Principle H: an easy, independent and accountable dispute resolution mechanism
cards.explanation: The framework's applicability note says principles A to G apply to all kinds of consumers and principle H applies only to retail consumers. Suitability, disclosure and data principles therefore reach corporate clients too.

cards.title: Who answers for conduct
cards.body:
**Board of directors**
- Approves the bank's own FTC framework and policies and sets up effective oversight.
- Creates a dedicated board committee, or widens the Board Risk Management Committee (BRMC), to oversee conduct and customer protection risk.

**Management committee** (group heads of business and control functions)
- Builds the internal FTC framework for board approval and keeps it under periodic review.
- Ensures SBP's Conduct Assessment Framework under BC&CPD Circular No. 3 of 2016, as amended, is implemented.
- Sets service quality benchmarks, the code of conduct and an escalation policy for conduct breaches.
- Meets at least twice a year and reports to the board committee at least twice a year.

**Conduct and FTC department**
- Preferably a dedicated unit. If not, FTC functions must work independently of business and operations.

**Internal audit**
- Assesses how far the BC&FRF and related policies are implemented.

items.label: Board of directors
items.detail: Approves the FTC framework and policies; sets up oversight.

items.label: Board committee or wider BRMC
items.detail: Asks management for compliance status; follows best practice in conduct and consumer protection.

items.label: Management committee
items.detail: Drives the FTC agenda, implements the CAF, sets the code of conduct and service benchmarks.

items.label: Conduct and FTC function
items.detail: Runs service quality, complaints and call-centre oversight, independent of sales.

items.label: Every employee and third-party worker
items.detail: Lives the code of conduct and is trained, competent and monitored.

cards.title: Whose job is it?
cards.prompt: Sort each duty to the body the BC&FRF gives it to.

items.text: Approve the bank's internal FTC framework and policies
Set up a board committee, or widen the BRMC, for conduct risk
Develop the internal FTC framework and procedures for approval
Ensure the 2016 Conduct Assessment Framework is implemented
Define the code of conduct for employees and third-party staff
Report progress on the PWD inclusion policy every half-year
Assess how far the BC&FRF has been implemented
Check, in regular audits, that Key Fact Statements are given and accurate
Audit the complaint handling mechanism at least once a year

cards.title: The 140 percent month
cards.setting: Video call between Islamabad and Karachi. 3:30 pm.

lines.text: Here is how my team is paid: a fixed salary, plus a bonus on policies and cards sold. The outsourced telesales agents get commission per sale. Simple.
Simple, and three of last month's Multan policies were cancelled within weeks. Two came with complaints that customers didn't know they were buying insurance.
The framework asks management to build FTC deliverables into employee KPIs, and to make sure the way we reward staff, third-party staff included, does not push behaviour that harms customers.
If I cut the bonus, my best people leave. If I keep it, I'm told it causes mis-selling. What do I put on the scorecard?
Let's design it together. Remember who the scorecard covers.

cards.title: Redesigning the sales scorecard
cards.situation: Kamran must propose a new quarterly scorecard for branch sales staff and the outsourced telesales agency that sells Kohsar Bank's cards and third-party insurance. The management committee will review it next week, and the board committee has asked how rewards support fair treatment.

choices.text: Keep volume as the only measure, but make every salesperson finish a conduct e-learning module first.
choices.outcome: Training is required, but it does not fix the incentive. The framework expects FTC deliverables inside KPIs and rewards that do not encourage harmful behaviour. A volume-only scorecard still pays people to push products.

choices.text: Add FTC measures (upheld complaints, cancellations, call-back results, persistency) weighted at least equal to volume, cover agency staff too, and link code breaches to discipline.
choices.outcome: This matches the framework: FTC goals sit in KPIs, rewards stop favouring harmful sales, third-party staff are covered, and breaches of the code lead to disciplinary action. It also meets the specific rule for third-party product sales, where quality and quantity must be at least equally weighted.

choices.text: Apply the new scorecard to permanent staff only, because the agency pays its own agents.
choices.outcome: The framework names third-party staff in the code of conduct and in the rule on rewards. Leaving agents on pure commission keeps the riskiest incentive in place for the people who make the most calls.

choices.text: Scrap every sales incentive for the year to be safe.
choices.outcome: No rule bans incentives. The requirement is that they do not reward behaviour that harms customers. Removing them all may be safe on paper but ignores the duty to put FTC deliverables into performance evaluation.

cards.title: Key terms in the Charter Room

cards.back: The exposure of customers to harmful outcomes caused by the financial institution's own practices.
Treating consumers in a way that is consistent with the principles and requirements of the BC&FRF.
Board Risk Management Committee. The board may widen its terms of reference to cover conduct and customer protection instead of creating a new committee.
SBP's framework under BC&CPD Circular No. 3 of 2016, as amended. The BC&FRF tells the management committee to ensure it is implemented.
Customer feedback that decision-making must take into account, especially for vulnerable customers or those in special circumstances.
Outsourced and agency workers. The code of conduct, the reward rules and the training duty all extend to them.

items.label: The test
items.right: Did the customer understand and get a suitable outcome?

items.label: Policies
items.right: Reviewed as markets, feedback and assessments change

cards.question: Kohsar Bank's management committee for conduct and FTC has met once this year. What is the minimum the BC&FRF requires?
options: It must meet at least twice a year and report to the board committee at least twice a year
It may set its own frequency as long as the board has approved it
It must meet every quarter and report to the full board every month
It must meet once a year, just before the annual accounts are approved
cards.explanation: Pillar 1 says the committee holds meetings at least bi-annually and that at least bi-annual performance reports go to the BRMC or the dedicated board committee. Quarterly reporting is required for some topics, such as call-centre performance, but not as the committee's minimum meeting rule.

cards.title: Real event: SBP launches the BC&FRF (October 2025)
cards.body:
**What happened.** On 17 October 2025 SBP announced the BC&FRF in a press release. It linked the framework to its Vision 2028 goal of stronger market conduct and consumer protection, and said it was finalised after consultation with consumers, financial institutions and industry bodies.

**What SBP highlighted.**
- Principles-based and rule-based obligations for banks, DFIs, EMIs and PSOs/PSPs, according to their scope of business.
- Coverage of the whole product lifecycle: design, pre-sale disclosure, service, complaints and ending the relationship.
- Two parts: outcome-based principles, and six pillars from governance to awareness and capacity building.

**What it means at Kohsar Bank.** The Multan complaint will be judged against the whole lifecycle: how the product was designed and approved, what was disclosed, how the sale was rewarded and how the complaint was handled. Before relying on an older SBP consumer circular, check whether the BC&FRF replaced it.

cards.title: Name the conflicts of interest
cards.body:
Pillar 1 asks every institution to identify and prevent or reduce conflicts of interest that can arise when it provides a product or service.

- Ask: who gains if the customer chooses this product, and is it the customer?
- Typical conflicts: commission paid by a product provider, conduct staff reporting to sales, and a salesperson checking his own sale.
- Write the conflict down, then remove it or control it (separate reporting lines, independent call-backs, balanced KPIs).
- If you cannot explain the control to a customer, it is probably not strong enough.

cards.title: Charter Room take-aways
items: The BC&FRF (BPRD Circular No. 4 of 2025) covers banks, DFIs, EMIs and PSOs/PSPs according to the business they are allowed to do.
Conduct risk is about harmful outcomes for customers caused by the institution's own practices.
Part One's principles A to H are obligations; principle H on dispute resolution applies to retail customers only.
The board approves the FTC framework and oversees conduct risk through a dedicated committee or a wider BRMC.
The management committee meets at least twice a year, implements the 2016 Conduct Assessment Framework and sets the code of conduct, KPIs and escalation policy.
Code of conduct, reward rules and regular training all extend to third-party staff.

cards.prompt: Think of one incentive, target or habit in your own team that could reward a sale more than a good outcome for the customer. What would you measure instead, and who would you need to convince?

quiz.question: Which description matches how the BC&FRF defines conduct risk?
options: The risk of SBP penalties for late regulatory returns
Losses the bank suffers when borrowers default on loans
Customers' exposure to harmful outcomes caused by the institution's own practices
The reputational damage a bank suffers when its name appears in negative press coverage
quiz.explanation: SBP frames conduct risk from the customer's side: detrimental outcomes for financial consumers caused by the institution's practices. Penalties and reputational damage can follow, but they are not the definition.

quiz.question: A digital bank argues that the BC&FRF does not apply to it because it has no branches. What is the best reply?
options: It applies only to its card business, because only cards are digital products
It applies only if SBP sends the digital bank a separate letter
Digital banks are expressly included in the framework's definition of banks
It applies only once the digital bank opens a physical branch
quiz.explanation: The framework applies to banks, DFIs, EMIs and PSOs/PSPs according to their scope of business, and the term banks includes commercial banks, foreign bank branches, microfinance banks and digital banks. Some branch-specific rules are relaxed for digital banks, but the framework itself applies.

quiz.question: Which pair correctly describes the two parts of the BC&FRF?
options: Part One: outcome-based principles A to H; Part Two: rule-based instructions in six pillars
Part One: guidance that is voluntary; Part Two: rules that are binding
Part One: rules for banks and DFIs; Part Two: separate rules for EMIs and payment service providers
Part One: six pillars; Part Two: a list of penalties for each pillar
quiz.explanation: Part One contains FTC outcome-based principles, which the framework calls obligations, and Part Two contains the rule-based instructions organised in six pillars. The principles are not voluntary guidance.

quiz.question: A branch charges a fee for a service that the bank cannot justify by its cost or by what peers charge. Which principle is most directly engaged?
options: Principle F, on reasonable charges supported by empirical analysis
Principle G, on lawful and secure processing of customer data
Principle A, on preventing market manipulation and collusion
Principle H, on independent and accountable dispute resolution
quiz.explanation: Principle F expects charges that match the service, are comparable with other banks for similar services and rest on empirical analysis. The other principles deal with ethics and collusion, data, and disputes.

quiz.question: Kohsar Bank's board does not want another committee. How can it meet the BC&FRF's oversight requirement?
options: Rely on the management committee alone and keep conduct risk off the board's agenda entirely
Ask the external auditor to oversee conduct risk once a year
Delegate conduct oversight entirely to the head of retail sales
Widen the BRMC's terms of reference to cover conduct and customer protection risk
quiz.explanation: Pillar 1 lets the board either create a dedicated committee or expand the BRMC's role, updating its terms of reference. Handing oversight to sales or to the external auditor does not satisfy the board-level duty.

quiz.question: Which task does the BC&FRF give to the management committee rather than to the board?
options: Ensuring the 2016 Conduct Assessment Framework is implemented
Setting up the board's own conduct oversight mechanism
Approving the bank's own internal FTC framework
Deciding whether to widen the BRMC's terms of reference
quiz.explanation: The management committee must ensure implementation of the CAF under BC&CPD Circular No. 3 of 2016, as amended. Approving the FTC framework and setting up board oversight belong to the board.

quiz.question: A bank says it cannot afford a separate conduct and FTC department. What does Pillar 1 require instead?
options: Conduct work can be added to the sales team's objectives
The bank must ask SBP for a written exemption from the requirement every year
FTC units must work independently of business and operations
The duty falls away until the bank reaches a set size
quiz.explanation: A dedicated department is preferred. If that is not feasible, the administrative units dealing with FTC functions must operate independently from the business and operations departments, so that sales does not mark its own homework.

quiz.question: An outsourced call-centre agent repeatedly misleads customers about card fees. What does the BC&FRF say about the code of conduct here?
options: The code covers payroll staff only, so the vendor alone must act
The bank must report the agent to SBP before taking any action
The code covers third-party staff, and the bank must take disciplinary action for breaches
The code applies to the agent only after he has finished the bank's full induction training programme
quiz.explanation: Management must define an employee code of conduct that includes third-party staff and must take appropriate disciplinary action for non-compliance. The bank cannot pass that responsibility entirely to the vendor.

quiz.question: Which statement about rewards matches the BC&FRF?
options: FTC goals belong in KPIs, and rewards must not encourage harm to customers
Rewards may follow volume alone as long as products are approved
Sales bonuses are banned outright for all staff who deal with retail customers
Incentives are a matter for HR and fall outside conduct rules
quiz.explanation: Pillar 1 asks management to integrate FTC deliverables into KPIs and to make sure the approach to rewarding employees, third-party staff included, does not incentivise poor conduct. It does not ban bonuses.

quiz.question: Who must the BC&FRF's regular training and awareness sessions on responsible conduct reach?
options: Customer-facing staff only, because they meet customers
New joiners only, during their first month at the bank
Employees at all levels, including third-party staff
Senior management only, because they set the culture
quiz.explanation: Pillar 1 requires regular training programmes and awareness sessions for employees at all levels, including third-party staff, on responsible conduct, FTC principles and customer-centricity.

sessions.title: Disclosure, Advertising and Fair Sales
sessions.summary: Apply Pillar 2's disclosure rules (languages, Key Fact Statements, terms, notice of changes, advertising and telemarketing) and Pillar 3's sales rules: suitability, bundling, free look-up periods, third-party products and the incentive structures that prevent mis-selling.
objectives: Apply the language, format and timing rules for terms and conditions, charges and changes
Use the Key Fact Statement and the credit card Summary Box correctly
Spot misleading advertising and unfair telemarketing practices
Apply suitability, bundling, free look-up, call-back and incentive rules to third-party product sales

cards.title: The 'free insurance' deposit
cards.setting: Kohsar Bank, Multan Cantt branch. Monday, 11:00 am.

lines.text: I came here with my commutation money and asked for a fixed deposit. The young man said I'd get a better plan with free insurance. Now I'm told I must pay premiums for ten years!
Sir, please sit. I'm Usman Baloch, the branch manager. Do you have the papers you signed?
A thick bundle in English. He showed me where to sign. No one read anything to me, and nobody called afterwards.
(on video from Islamabad) Mr Ahmed, thank you for coming in. We will look at every step of that sale, starting with what you were shown before you signed.
The salesperson says it's on the system as an investment-linked plan, and the customer signed the risk undertaking.
Then let's test it against the rules. What should a customer see, in which language, and when? And what should have happened after the sale?

cards.title: Clear information before the customer commits

scenes.heading: Two languages
scenes.narration: Account forms, terms and conditions, charges and explanations of the customer's responsibilities must be given in both Urdu and English, in clear text of at least font size 11. Regional languages are encouraged.

scenes.heading: The Key Fact Statement
scenes.narration: Prospective customers get a Key Fact Statement, the KFS, for deposit and financing products so they can compare offers. At account opening or before a loan is disbursed, the customer and an authorised officer both sign it, and the customer keeps a copy.

scenes.heading: Terms before the contract
scenes.narration: Terms and conditions are given at or before the contract, with a signed duplicate for the customer. They must show all charges, how mark-up is calculated, whether the rate is fixed or variable, and how to complain.

scenes.heading: Changes with notice
scenes.narration: If terms, mark-up or charges change, the customer must be told at least thirty days in advance. Changes forced by law or regulatory instructions are notified immediately, and customers can leave without penalty within the notice period.

scenes.heading: Honest advertising
scenes.narration: Adverts must be clear, fair and not misleading. Nothing is called free if any fee applies, promotions state how long they run, and deposit adverts show the annualised expected rate of return.

items.label: Advert and sales material
items.detail: Clear, not misleading, key terms readable; points to fuller product information.

items.label: Key Fact Statement
items.detail: Available in branches, on the website and in digital channels, for comparison.

items.label: Terms, charges and schedule
items.detail: Given at or before the contract; schedule of charges in branches and online.

items.label: Signing
items.detail: KFS signed by customer and authorised officer; duplicate copies to the customer.

items.label: Statements and alerts
items.detail: Instant alerts for debits, credits and rejected transactions; periodic statements.

items.label: Changes and exit
items.detail: At least 30 days' notice of changes; closure confirmed within 2 working days.

cards.title: Compliant or red flag?
cards.prompt: Sort each advert or sales practice.

items.text: A 'zero-fee' card whose annual fee appears only in a footnote
A deposit advert stating the annualised expected rate of return
'Your overdraft limit rises next month unless you tell us not to'
A promotion stating it runs from 1 to 31 March and linking to its terms
A risk warning printed in tiny type that few can read
A short radio spot telling listeners where to find full product details
A marketing call to a customer on the bank's 'Don't call' list
A telesales agent giving her name and the bank's name before the pitch
Offering, explaining and closing an insurance sale on one first call

cards.question: Kohsar Bank wants to raise its charge for a standing instruction service. What notice does the BC&FRF require?
options: At least 30 days before the change, unless it results from a change in law or regulatory instructions
At least 7 days before the change, by a notice displayed in branches
No notice, provided the new charge is in the updated schedule of charges
Notice within 30 days after the change, in the next account statement
cards.explanation: Pillar 2 requires at least thirty days' advance notice of changes to terms, mark-up or other charges, and immediate notice where the change follows from the legal framework or regulatory instructions. Customers may also exit without penalty within the notice period.

cards.title: Suitability, bundling and the right to change your mind
cards.body:
**Suitability (Pillar 3)**
- Products are designed and sold on the basis of a customer needs assessment, matching risk tolerance, financial capacity and objectives.
- Products must not unfairly disadvantage a group of customers, especially vulnerable segments.
- New products, including their marketing and distribution, need approval from the FTC management committee, with monitoring in place.

**Bundling**
- Only on the customer's request or explicit, verifiable consent, with separate disclosures for each product.
- Bundling with a third party's product, such as bancassurance, is prohibited.

**Product conversions**
- At least 30 days' notice, a standard consent form in English and Urdu, and a recorded call-back after 24 hours but within 3 days.

**Free look-up**
- Subscription services (such as SMS alerts or credit shield) get a free look-up of at least 15 days; fees are reversed within five working days of an opt-out.

items.label: Notice of changes
items.detail: Minimum advance notice of changes to terms, mark-up or charges, and of product conversions.

items.label: Subscription free look-up
items.detail: Minimum free look-up for subscription services; fees reversed within five working days.

items.label: Third-party free look-up
items.detail: Minimum for third-party investment products other than insurance.

items.label: Bancassurance free look-up
items.detail: Free look-up for bancassurance, in line with SECP rules.

items.label: Call-back records
items.detail: Keep third-party product call-back records 7 years or to maturity, whichever is later.

items.label: Closure confirmed
items.detail: Confirm the termination or closure of a contract to the customer.

lines.text: I pulled the file. The call-back confirmation was made by the same salesperson, on the same afternoon he sold the policy.
He's my top performer. The insurer also sent him on an incentive trip last year for exceeding targets.

That's two problems. Call-backs must be done by staff outside sales who earn nothing from these products, and never on the day of sale. And staff may not take incentives directly from the product provider.
Mr Ahmed is back at the branch today. He just wants his money in a fixed deposit, as he asked.
Then let's decide what we do for him first, and fix our process second.

cards.title: Mr Ahmed wants out
cards.situation: Bashir Ahmed, a 64-year-old retired teacher, is at the branch twelve working days after buying an investment-linked bancassurance plan. He wants to cancel and put his money in a fixed deposit. The policy documents have not reached him yet. His suitability record shows 'high risk appetite' and 'long-term horizon', which he says nobody asked him about.

choices.text: Process the cancellation now through the branch, without waiting for the policy documents and without charges, log a mis-selling complaint in the CMS, and open a review of the sale.
choices.outcome: Right. The free look-up for bancassurance is fourteen working days, banks must help customers cancel through all channels without waiting for policy documents, and an exit at this stage should carry no charge. Logging the complaint starts the root-cause work on suitability and call-backs.

choices.text: Tell him to contact the insurance company, because the bank only distributed the product.
choices.outcome: The bank cannot step aside. The BC&FRF requires banks to facilitate cancellation through all available channels and to help resolve complaints about third-party products they sold.

choices.text: Offer to switch him into a lower-premium plan from the same insurer instead of cancelling.
choices.outcome: He has asked to cancel within the free look-up period. Pushing another product repeats the original mis-selling problem and ignores the customer's stated need.

choices.text: Cancel the plan, but wait until the documents arrive so the insurer can confirm the refund amount first.
choices.outcome: Cancelling is right, but waiting is not. The framework tells banks to facilitate cancellation without waiting for delivery of the policy documents.

cards.back: Covers due diligence on the provider, the sales model, the staff incentive structure and risk mitigants.
A central unit verifies every sales proposal. It must have no incentive linked to sales of these products.
Suitability assessed against approved criteria before the sale; the record is kept until one year after the product matures.
Requests from senior citizens, widows, illiterate persons, persons with disabilities and pensioners need approval at least at Regional Head level.
A distinct document: the bank is only a distributor, how returns work, encashment penalties, claims and redress; in Urdu or English as the customer chooses.
A scripted call by staff outside sales, never on the day of sale, confirming the customer's information and understanding.

cards.title: Incentives that do not reward mis-selling
cards.prompt: Match each rule to what it requires.

pairs.right: Measures of sales quality and of volume carry at least equal weight
Incentive structures based on policies staying in force promote responsible sales
No employee may receive incentives directly from the insurer or product provider
The management committee reviews cancellations, persistency and mis-selling complaints
Customer surveys and mystery shopping at least once a year for third-party sales
Staff verifying sales proposals have no incentive linked to these sales

cards.question: A customer applying for a personal loan says he is happy to sign consent for a third-party life policy to be bundled with it. What does the BC&FRF say?
options: The bundle is allowed if the Regional Head approves the case
The bundle is allowed if the KFS for the loan mentions the policy
The bank may not bundle its products with a third party's product such as bancassurance
The bundle is allowed once the customer signs explicit, verifiable consent
cards.explanation: Explicit, verifiable consent allows a bank to bundle its own products, with separate disclosures for each. Bundling with products issued by a third party, such as bancassurance, is prohibited outright.

cards.title: Selling a third-party investment product properly
cards.prompt: Put the steps of a compliant sale in order.
steps: State your official identity and that the bank acts only as distributor
Assess suitability against the bank's approved criteria
Explain the risks, give the basic fact sheet and take the customer's undertaking
Send the proposal to the independent control function for verification
Make the call-back confirmation through staff outside sales, not on the day of sale
Honour any free look-up cancellation without charges

cards.title: Kohsar case: what went wrong in Multan
cards.body:
Zara's review of Mr Ahmed's sale found these gaps against the BC&FRF:

- **Suitability:** the record showed a high risk appetite that the customer never stated. Products that pay off only in the long run must not go to customers without the capacity for that risk.
- **Vulnerable buyer:** as a pensioner and senior citizen, his purchase needed approval at least at Regional Head level and the branch manager's undertaking that features were explained. Neither was on file.
- **Language:** documents were in English only; he should have had the basic fact sheet in the language he chose.
- **'Free insurance':** a product cannot be presented as free when charges apply.
- **Call-back:** done by the seller on the day of sale, which the rules forbid.
- **Incentives:** volume-only bonuses and a provider-funded trip.

**Fixes:** cancel and refund, retrain the branch team, rebalance the scorecard, and move call-backs to an independent team.

cards.title: Telemarketing hygiene
cards.body:
Pillar 2 sets clear rules for marketing staff, whether on payroll or third-party:

- Disclose your official identity before or during the contact.
- Give complete, accurate information; never claim features the bank does not offer.
- Keep and respect a 'Don't call' list that every marketer can see.
- Never offer, market and sell on a single call.
- The bank runs surprise checks such as mystery shopping at least twice a year. Anyone found making false claims or calling 'Don't call' customers faces remedial and disciplinary action, and the customer is informed.

cards.title: Glass Counter take-aways
items: Forms, terms and charges come in Urdu and English, in readable type, before or at the contract, with signed copies for the customer.
The KFS is signed by the customer and an authorised officer; credit cards need a signed Summary Box before issue.
Changes need at least 30 days' notice, immediate notice if law or regulation forces them, and customers can exit without penalty within that period.
No 'free' claims when fees apply, no automatic credit offers, no single-call sales and no calls to 'Don't call' customers.
Bundling with third-party products such as bancassurance is prohibited; own-product bundles need explicit, verifiable consent.
Third-party sales need suitability checks, independent verification, call-backs by non-sales staff and incentives where quality weighs at least as much as volume.

cards.prompt: Pick one product you sell or support. Could a customer who reads only Urdu, or who is in a hurry, explain its main charges and risks after your conversation? What would you change in how you present it?

quiz.question: What does Pillar 2 require for the account opening form, terms and conditions and schedule of charges given to a retail customer?
options: English text only, with an Urdu summary on request
Urdu or English, whichever the branch manager chooses
Clear text in both Urdu and English, at least font size 11
Any language at all, as long as the customer signs a declaration of understanding
quiz.explanation: Pillar 2 requires this information in clear text of at least font size 11, in both Urdu and English, and encourages regional languages as well.

quiz.question: At account opening, who must sign the deposit Key Fact Statement?
options: Only the branch manager, as proof the KFS was offered
Nobody; the KFS is published on the website instead
Both the customer and an authorised officer, with a copy for the customer
Only the customer, and the bank keeps the only copy
quiz.explanation: The KFS must be signed by the authorised officer and the customer at account opening or before disbursement, kept under the record retention policy, and a duplicate given to the customer.

quiz.question: A card advert says 'No annual fee' in large type, with a footnote that a yearly service charge applies. What is the main problem?
options: The headline is fine, because the footnote is printed at font size 8 or larger as required
There is no problem because the charge is disclosed in the footnote
A product cannot be presented as free or no-cost when any fee, by any name, applies
The advert only needs the annualised rate of return to be shown
quiz.explanation: Pillar 2 bars presenting a product as free or no-cost if any fee or implied charge is attached, whatever it is called. Font-size rules for footnotes do not cure a misleading headline.

quiz.question: Kohsar Bank plans to raise the credit limit of selected cardholders automatically next month unless they reply to decline. Is this allowed?
options: Yes, as long as the customers receive the offer by SMS at least 30 days before the increase
No; an offer of credit may not take effect automatically unless the customer declines
Yes, for customers who have never missed a card payment
Yes, if the new limit is shown in the next statement of account
quiz.explanation: Pillar 2 forbids offers of credit, including increases to overdraft or credit facilities, that come into existence automatically unless the customer declines. The customer must actively accept.

quiz.question: A bank converts customers from one savings product to another. Which set of steps does Pillar 3 require?
options: Board approval of the conversion, with no need for customer consent
A notice on the website and a call-back on the same day as consent
7 days' notice by SMS, followed by an automatic switch for every customer who does not reply in time
30 days' notice, bilingual consent forms, and a recorded call-back between 24 hours and 3 days later
quiz.explanation: For conversions the bank must inform customers at least 30 days ahead, obtain verifiable consent on standardised forms in English and Urdu, and run a recorded call-back with an approved script after 24 hours but within 3 days of consent.

quiz.question: A customer subscribes to a credit shield service and opts out on day 10. What does Pillar 3 require?
options: Allow the opt-out and reverse any fee within five working days of the request
Charge a fair cancellation fee, because the service was already active for ten days
Keep the fee but stop the service at the end of the billing cycle
Refer the request to SBP's Consumer Protection Department for a decision
quiz.explanation: Subscription-based services must have a free look-up of at least 15 days. A customer who opts out in that period must be unsubscribed and any charges reversed within five working days.

quiz.question: Which person is best placed to make the call-back confirmation for a bancassurance sale?
options: The salesperson who closed the sale, because she knows the customer and the product best
An agent employed by the insurer that issued the policy
A trained officer outside sales who earns no incentive from third-party products
The branch manager, on the same day the policy was sold
quiz.explanation: The call-back must be made by a function or staff not involved in selling these products and not receiving incentives from them, and not on the day of sale. Someone who gains from the sale cannot test it independently.

quiz.question: A widow asks to invest in a third-party investment product at a branch. What extra step does Pillar 3 require?
options: Regional Head approval at least, plus the branch manager's undertaking
A referral to SBP's Consumer Protection Department before the sale
A cap limiting the investment to a fixed share of her deposits
A second signature from an adult family member confirming that they agree with the investment
quiz.explanation: Investments in third-party products by senior citizens, widows, illiterate persons, differently-abled persons and pensioners must be approved at least at Regional Head level, and the branch manager signs an undertaking that features and terms were explained.

quiz.question: How must performance of staff selling insurance through the bank be measured?
options: Persistency is ignored because policies are the insurer's responsibility
Only proven complaints count, so that measures stay objective
Measures of sales quality and quantity carry at least equal weight
Volume of premiums sold is the main measure, with quality as a tie-breaker
quiz.explanation: Pillar 3 says staff must not be incentivised to sell insurance in ways contrary to fair outcomes, that incentives should be based on persistency, and that quality and quantity parameters must be at least equally weighted.

quiz.question: What must marketing personnel, including third-party marketers, do before or during a meeting with a prospective customer?
options: Collect the customer's OTP to verify identity
Disclose their official identity
Ask the customer to sign a waiver of the free look-up
Offer at least two products in the same conversation
quiz.explanation: Pillar 2 requires marketing staff, on payroll or third-party, to disclose their official identity and give complete, accurate information. Banks must never ask for OTPs verbally, and waiving the free look-up is not a sales step.

sessions.title: Responsible Lending, Fair Collection and Inclusion
sessions.summary: Apply Pillar 3's financing rules (prudent lending, rates, prepayment, repayment allocation and guarantors), conduct debt collection within the BC&FRF's notice and behaviour limits, and serve persons with disabilities, pensioners and other vulnerable customers with the care the framework requires.
objectives: Apply SBP's rules on fair credit terms, fixed and floating rates, prepayment and repayment allocation
Run debt collection within the BC&FRF's notice, contact, conduct and eCIB-reporting rules
Serve persons with disabilities using the bank's PWD policy and model-branch standards
Give pensioners, senior citizens and other vulnerable customers the extra care the framework requires

cards.title: Calls to the office
cards.setting: Complaints unit, Kohsar Bank, Gulberg, Lahore. Tuesday, 9:40 am.

lines.text: New complaint from Hyderabad. A car-loan borrower missed two instalments. The collection agency phoned his employer, and his brother-in-law at ten at night.
That agency is outsourced. They're paid a percentage of what they recover, so they chase hard.
Outsourced doesn't mean out of our hands. The framework says we monitor collection agencies, train collection staff, and we never contact a borrower's employer.
(joining from Multan) And I have the opposite problem. A wheelchair user couldn't get up our steps yesterday, and a deaf customer left because nobody could understand her.
Two sides of the same pillar: fair treatment. Today we fix how we lend and collect, and how we serve customers who need more from us.
Where do we start? The borrower is waiting for an answer.

scenes.heading: Prudent and affordable
scenes.narration: Banks extend financing prudently, in line with SBP's instructions and their own policies, so that it matches the customer's borrowing needs and financial capacity. Staff must make sure the borrower understands the main terms.

scenes.heading: Fixed or floating, clearly
scenes.narration: Loan documents say whether the rate is fixed, floating or both. A fixed rate cannot rise during the tenor. For a floating rate, the margin over the benchmark, such as KIBOR, is stated and cannot be increased. No clause may let the bank change the rate on its own.

scenes.heading: Schedules
scenes.narration: The customer gets a full amortisation schedule with the offer letter, and a new one whenever a floating rate is reset. Statements of outstanding principal and mark-up follow at least twice a year.

scenes.heading: Early repayment
scenes.narration: Customers have the right to repay early. Any prepayment penalty may not exceed the bank's actual loss or cost, and third-party costs such as valuation or repossession are recovered only at actual cost.

scenes.heading: Reaching out early
scenes.narration: The management committee must set up a process to identify borrowers who have, or may soon have, repayment difficulties, and reach out to them with suitable options or guidance.

cards.title: The fair collection clock
cards.caption: Contact is never at inconvenient times, and collectors always state their name, the bank and the purpose of the call.

items.label: First missed payment
items.detail: The account becomes overdue; reminders and help to repay start.

items.label: Notice before any visit
items.detail: An acknowledged notice by letter and SMS or email before visiting home or business, or repossessing a vehicle.

items.label: Borrower out of contact
items.detail: If there is no contact 30 days after the first missed due date, information may be sought from next of kin or nominee.

items.label: Before eCIB reporting
items.detail: Intimation by letter and SMS or email, explaining the impact, with at least 15 days to reconcile or settle.

items.label: Visit reports kept
items.detail: Keep visit reports at least six months, or longer under the bank's retention policy.

items.text: Calling the borrower at 11 pm because he doesn't answer by day
Phoning the borrower's employer to press for payment
Visiting the home after a duly acknowledged 14-day notice
Telling neighbours about the debt to shame the borrower
Opening a call with your name, the bank's name and the purpose
Contacting the nominee after 30 days of no contact since the first missed payment
Repossessing a car before the borrower can remove his belongings
Setting off a deposit against the loan without informing the customer
Sending recovery letters that show the officer's designation, phone and office address

cards.question: A borrower has a personal loan and a credit card balance with Kohsar Bank, and pays an amount without saying how to apply it. What does the BC&FRF require?
options: Apply it first to the facility with the higher annual percentage rate
Apply it first to the facility that is longest overdue
Apply it first to the facility with the larger outstanding balance
Split it equally between the two facilities
cards.explanation: Without instructions, repayments are appropriated first against the loan with the higher APR. Even when the customer gives instructions that would cost more, the bank should guide the customer and not profit from his lack of knowledge.

cards.title: What the bank must build around collectors

items.label: The margin
items.right: Cannot be increased during the tenor

items.label: Schedule
items.left: Full amortisation schedule with the offer letter
items.right: New schedule each time the rate resets

lines.text: We have a ramp quote, but head office says it can wait until the branch is renovated next year.
It can't. Every bank must build ramps at all new and existing places of business, apart from mobile banking units, and list those branches on its website.
(visiting with a friend) My friend Rafiq is blind. Last time a clerk told him he needed a sighted relative to open an account at all.
That's wrong too. A visually impaired person cannot be refused an individual account, and a literate blind customer must not be treated as illiterate.
Then my team needs more than a ramp. They need training.

cards.title: The deaf customer comes back
cards.situation: Nadira, a deaf customer, returns to the Multan Cantt branch with her nephew to open a savings account. She writes that she wants to deal with the bank herself, not through her nephew. The branch has no sign-language-trained staff, and the nearest model branch is in another city. The teller suggests the nephew simply sign everything on her behalf.

choices.text: Serve her directly in writing and through the bank's sign-language interpretation service, including any digital or video option, give her priority service, and note the training gap for Usman's action plan.
choices.outcome: Right. The PWD policy must provide sign-language interpretation, including by digital or virtual means, with priority and due care. The customer's wish to act for herself is respected, and the missing training is fixed at its root.

choices.text: Let the nephew sign as her representative, since she came with him.
choices.outcome: This takes the decision away from a customer who wants to act for herself and risks exploitation. Nothing in her disability prevents her from operating her own account.

choices.text: Ask her to travel to the nearest model branch, where staff know sign language.
choices.outcome: Model branches add specialised service, but every branch must serve persons with disabilities with due care. Sending her away is a barrier, not an accommodation.

choices.text: Open the account in writing today, but tell her that future visits must be at the model branch.
choices.outcome: Opening the account is right, but limiting her to one branch is not. The policy aims at access across the network, with sign-language help available through digital means.

cards.back: Each bank needs a PWD policy and strategy approved by its board, covering customers and employees, including women with disabilities.
Mandatory at all new and existing places of business, except mobile banking units, with a list of such branches on the website.
A minimum list of forms, such as the account opening form and deposit slip, available in braille at controlling offices.
Designated in each province according to the bank's branch network, with trained staff and accessible ATMs, counters and lockers.
Model branches give at least one staff member basic sign-language awareness and training, and offer interpretation services.
Banks collaborate so that at least one branch in an area has a talking ATM for visually impaired customers.

cards.title: Model branches per province
cards.caption: Model branches serve persons with disabilities while also serving the general public.

items.label: 25 to 200 branches
items.detail: A bank or DFI of this size designates one model branch in each province.

items.label: 201 to 500 branches
items.detail: Two model branches in each province.

items.label: 501 to 1,000 branches
items.detail: Four model branches in each province.

items.label: Over 1,000 branches
items.detail: Six model branches in each province.

cards.title: Extra care for vulnerable customers
cards.prompt: Match each customer group to a protection in the BC&FRF.

pairs.right: Special assistance at account opening; pensions credited without delay
No inter-switch fee on ATM transactions under the government-backed scheme
Cannot be refused an individual account; literate customers not treated as illiterate
Extra care, with their understanding given ample weight
Drinking water and shelter from heat and rain
Approval at least at Regional Head level

cards.question: A guarantor has signed for a business loan that has not yet been disbursed and now wants to withdraw. What does Pillar 3 allow?
options: The guarantor may withdraw only with the borrower's written consent
The guarantor may never withdraw once the guarantee is signed
The guarantor may withdraw only after the first instalment is paid
The guarantor may withdraw before the credit is provided, by acknowledged written notice or email
cards.explanation: Pillar 3 lets guarantors withdraw from the guarantee before the credit is provided, by acknowledged written notice or email. Banks must also tell guarantors their obligations, their right to independent advice and give them the contracts and offer letter.

cards.title: Kohsar case: the Hyderabad car loan
cards.body:
**The facts.** A borrower missed two instalments. The outsourced agency, paid on recoveries, called his employer and called a relative late at night. No acknowledged notice had been sent before an officer visited his house.

**Against the BC&FRF:**
- Contacting the employer is forbidden in all cases.
- Calls at inconvenient times, and intruding on relatives' privacy, breach the conduct rules.
- A visit needs a duly acknowledged notice of at least 14 days by letter and SMS or email.
- The bank, not the agency, answers for monitoring and training collectors.

**What Kohsar did.**
- Apologised and recorded the complaint in the CMS.
- Suspended the agency's work on the case and reviewed its call logs.
- Updated the agency contract: code of lawful conduct, training records, monitoring and penalties.
- Offered the borrower a meeting to discuss a repayment plan, in writing and in line with the restructuring policy.

cards.title: Reach out before the default
cards.body:
The framework expects banks to spot borrowers at risk of repayment difficulty and contact them proactively.

- Watch early signals: salary credits stopping, partial payments, rising card utilisation.
- Set due dates that suit the borrower, for example close to a salaried customer's pay date.
- Teach customers how repayments work so they avoid unnecessary charges.
- Record any restructuring negotiation in writing, under the bank's approved policy.
- A helpful call at day five beats a recovery visit at day sixty.

cards.title: Recovery Road take-aways
items: Lend prudently to need and capacity; fixed rates and floating margins cannot be raised during the tenor, and no clause may allow one-sided rate changes.
Prepayment penalties may not exceed the bank's actual loss or cost; unclear repayments go first to the highest-APR facility.
Collections need a 14-day acknowledged notice before visits, polite contact at reasonable times, and never a call to the borrower's employer.
Borrowers get at least 15 days' notice before overdue amounts are reported to eCIB.
The bank trains, monitors and answers for its collection staff and agencies.
PWD policy, ramps everywhere, model branches, sign language and braille, plus extra care for pensioners, senior citizens and other vulnerable customers.

cards.prompt: Think of a customer you served who struggled: with a disability, with literacy, with age or with debt. What one change in your branch or team would have made that visit fair and dignified?

quiz.question: A fixed-rate auto loan has three years left. Funding costs have risen sharply. What may the bank do with the rate?
options: Raise it after giving the borrower 30 days' written notice
Raise it, provided the borrower signs a revised offer letter at the time of the increase
Raise it by the same amount that KIBOR has moved
Nothing; a fixed rate cannot be increased during the tenor of the loan
quiz.explanation: Pillar 3 says the rate on fixed-rate financing shall not be increased during the tenor, and agreements may not contain clauses that change the rate unilaterally.

quiz.question: For a floating-rate home loan priced at KIBOR plus a margin, what is the bank not allowed to do?
options: Reset the rate when KIBOR changes on the agreed date
Issue a new amortisation schedule after a reset
State the margin over the benchmark in the documents
Increase the margin during the tenor of the loan
quiz.explanation: For floating rates, the bank must specify the margin over the benchmark and may not increase it during the tenor. Resetting with the benchmark and issuing a new schedule are expected, not forbidden.

quiz.question: A customer repays a personal loan early. The bank's actual cost of early repayment is Rs 8,000. Which penalty is consistent with the BC&FRF?
options: A flat 5 percent of the outstanding balance, as the contract says
Any penalty up to Rs 8,000, the bank's actual loss or cost
Six months of mark-up, to protect the bank's expected income
No early repayment is allowed during the first year
quiz.explanation: Customers have the right to repay early. A bank may charge a penalty, but it may not exceed the actual loss or cost to the bank. Contract terms cannot override that limit.

quiz.question: Before visiting a defaulting borrower's home to negotiate recovery, what must the bank do?
options: Serve at least 14 days' duly acknowledged notice by letter and SMS or email
Call the borrower's employer to arrange a convenient time
Obtain a court order allowing the visit
Report the overdue amount to eCIB the same day
quiz.explanation: Pillar 3 requires a minimum 14-day acknowledged notice through letter and SMS or email before a visit to the residence or business, and the same applies before repossessing a leased vehicle.

quiz.question: A borrower's overdue amount is about to be reported to eCIB. What must happen first?
options: Nothing, because eCIB reporting is a regulatory duty
An intimation by letter and SMS or email explaining the impact, with at least 15 days to settle
A notice on the branch board listing defaulters by name
A phone call on the day of reporting, recorded for evidence
quiz.explanation: Before reporting an overdue to eCIB, banks must send an intimation letter and SMS or email, explain the implications and allow at least 15 days for reconciliation or settlement.

quiz.question: A borrower has not been reachable for 30 days after the due date of his first missed payment. What does Pillar 3 allow?
options: Visiting his home without any further notice
Obtaining necessary information from his next of kin, nominee or a supplementary cardholder
Publishing his name in a newspaper notice
Calling his employer to confirm he still works there
quiz.explanation: If the borrower is not in contact for 30 days after the first missed due date, the bank may obtain necessary information from next of kin, a nominee, a supplementary cardholder or a third party. Contacting the employer stays forbidden.

quiz.question: Kohsar Bank outsources collections to an agency. Which statement reflects the BC&FRF?
options: The bank must use qualified, trained collection staff and monitor the agency regularly
The agency's own code replaces the bank's code of lawful conduct
Agency staff may contact the borrower's employer if the borrower agreed to this in the loan contract
The bank is responsible only for its own payroll collection officers
quiz.explanation: The bank must frame a code of lawful conduct for recovery staff, engage qualified staff and train them, run a complaint mechanism against collection staff and monitor staff and agencies. Employer contact is barred in all cases.

quiz.question: Which PWD measure does the BC&FRF make mandatory for every bank and DFI, not only model branches?
options: Height-adjusted counters and voice-enabled ATMs in every branch
Ramps at all new and existing places of business, except mobile banking units
Dedicated parking spaces reserved for persons with disabilities outside every single branch
A sign-language interpreter on site in every branch
quiz.explanation: Ramps are mandatory at all newly opened and existing places of business, excluding mobile banking units. Height-adjusted counters, voice ATMs and dedicated parking are listed among model-branch standards.

quiz.question: A bank has 650 branches. How many model branches for persons with disabilities must it designate in each province?
options: One
Three
Two
Four
quiz.explanation: The scale is one model branch per province for 25 to 200 branches, two for 201 to 500, four for 501 to 1,000 and six for more than 1,000.

quiz.question: A literate blind customer wants a debit card. What do the BC&FRF's guidelines for visually impaired customers say?
options: The card may be issued only to a sighted joint account holder, never to the blind customer
The card is barred because ATM use carries too much risk
The card may be issued only with a court-appointed guardian
The bank must not deny the card against a duly witnessed undertaking
quiz.explanation: Annexure 3B says banks shall not deny ATM or debit cards to literate visually impaired account holders against a duly witnessed undertaking, and must not equate literate blind customers with illiterate ones.

sessions.title: Complaints, SBP Sunwai and the Banking Mohtasib
sessions.summary: Handle complaints the way Pillar 5 requires: recognise them, log every one in the complaint management system, acknowledge, classify and resolve within set times, reply in writing with reasons, and explain the escalation routes through SBP's Sunwai portal and the Banking Mohtasib under Part IVA of the Banking Companies Ordinance 1962.
objectives: Recognise a complaint under the BC&FRF definition and log it in the CMS whatever the channel
Apply the acknowledgement, classification, timeline and final-reply rules
Explain escalation through SBP's Sunwai portal and the Banking Mohtasib, including the BCO 1962 time limits
Use complaint data, call-centre controls and care for vulnerable complainants to fix root causes

cards.title: The complaints that never existed
cards.setting: Complaints unit, Lahore, and Multan Cantt branch on video. Monday.

lines.text: Our system shows four complaints from Multan Cantt last quarter. The branch register shows thirty-one.
Most were sorted at the counter in ten minutes. Why fill the system with things we already fixed?
Because SBP sees our complaint returns, our auditors test them, and a pattern of 'small' issues is how we find a broken process.
(letter read out by Mehwish) 'I complained about my policy six weeks ago and received no written answer. I have now complained on SBP's Sunwai portal.'
And if our reply doesn't satisfy him, the next stop is the Banking Mohtasib.
So what exactly counts as a complaint, and what clock starts when one arrives?

scenes.heading: What counts
scenes.narration: A complaint is any written, digital or verbal expression of dissatisfaction alleging financial loss, inconvenience or distress caused by a bank's product or service, or by a third party it has outsourced to. It must never be downgraded to a service request.

scenes.heading: Log every one
scenes.narration: Every complaint, whatever the channel, goes into the complaint management system, the CMS. That includes complaints from SBP's Sunwai portal and those forwarded by SBP or the Banking Mohtasib, and those fixed at the branch.

scenes.heading: Acknowledge and track
scenes.narration: The customer gets a tracking number by SMS and email, never by phone call alone, and an acknowledgement within 48 hours that explains the process, the timeline and whom to contact.

scenes.heading: Resolve on time
scenes.narration: Minor complaints are resolved within three or seven working days. Major ones get an interim reply after ten working days and are disposed of within fifteen days; fraud cases get a final reply within thirty days of lodging.

scenes.heading: Reasons and the next forum
scenes.narration: If a complaint is declined, the written reply gives the reasons and evidence and names the alternate forum with its contact details, for banks usually the Banking Mohtasib.

items.label: Receive through any channel
items.detail: Branch, call centre, email, website, e-form, mail, complaint box, ATM hotline, Sunwai.

items.label: Log in the CMS
items.detail: Name, CNIC or passport, product, nature, dates; kept as a permanent record.

items.label: Tracking number and acknowledgement
items.detail: Tracking number by SMS and email; acknowledgement within 48 hours.

items.label: Classify and resolve
items.detail: Minor (3 or 7 working days) or major (interim reply, then disposal).

items.label: Final reply in writing
items.detail: Reasons and evidence if declined, plus the second forum's details; Urdu complaint, Urdu reply.

items.label: Analyse and fix
items.detail: Root causes by product and channel feed product, process and training changes.

cards.title: Complaint or service request?
cards.prompt: Apply the BC&FRF definition of a complaint.

items.text: 'I was charged twice for my card renewal and want my money back'
'Please send me a new cheque book'
'The teller was rude and made me wait an hour for no reason'
'What is your profit rate on a one-year term deposit?'
'My statement hasn't arrived for two half-years in a row'
'Please update my mailing address to my new flat'
'Your agent called my office about my loan and embarrassed me'
'How do I activate internet banking?'

cards.question: A customer complains by phone at 8 pm on a Thursday. By when, at the latest, must the acknowledgement reach the customer?
options: Within 7 working days, together with the final resolution
Within 15 working days, as part of the interim reply
There is no deadline as long as a tracking number was given on the call
Within 48 hours, and for an after-hours complaint no later than the following working day
cards.explanation: Pillar 5 says an after-hours complaint is acknowledged no later than the next working day, and in any case within 48 hours, by SMS, email, recorded line or mail. The tracking number itself must go by SMS and email, not by call alone.

cards.title: Timelines and quality rules
cards.body:
**Classify in the CMS**
- **Minor:** needs 7 working days or less. Banks may split it into 3-day issues (statement not delivered, activation, cheque book, change of address) and 7-day issues (misbehaviour, system faults, repayment or settlement disputes). If an extraordinary investigation is needed, send an interim reply and resolve within 15 working days.
- **Major:** needs more than 7 working days (fraud, embezzlement, repayment disputes). Interim reply after 10 working days; disposal within 15 days; fraud cases get a final reply within 30 days of lodging.
- **Domestic credit card disputes:** never more than 45 working days, and no mark-up charged on the disputed amount during the investigation.

**Quality rules**
- Final replies in writing, especially declines; a complaint in Urdu gets a reply in Urdu.
- An escalation ladder for complaints not resolved in time.
- Compensation for delay in giving relief.
- Extra care for vulnerable complainants; pensioners and senior citizens handled on priority.

items.label: Definition
items.left: Resolvable in 7 working days or less

items.label: Typical issues
items.left: Statement not received, cheque book, rude service

items.label: Interim reply
items.left: Only if extraordinary investigation is needed

items.label: Outer limit
items.right: 15 days; fraud final reply within 30 days

cards.title: Bashir goes to the Mohtasib
cards.setting: Conduct review, Islamabad. Six weeks later.

lines.text: We gave Mr Ahmed his refund, but he also wants compensation for the delay and the stress. He has written to the Banking Mohtasib.
Can he do that? We've already refunded him.
He can. He told us in writing first, and he wasn't satisfied with our answer. The Mohtasib can mediate, and if that fails, direct us to pay reasonable compensation.
And if the Mohtasib rules against us, we have thirty days to appeal to the SBP Governor, or forty days to implement.
Then let's decide now how we respond, before the hearing notice arrives.

cards.title: The Mohtasib's finding
cards.situation: The Banking Mohtasib finds Mr Ahmed's complaint partly justified. After mediation fails, the finding directs Kohsar Bank to pay him reasonable compensation and to improve its bancassurance sales process. Kamran thinks the amount is too high. The board committee asks Zara for advice.

choices.text: Decide within 30 days whether there are real grounds to appeal to the SBP Governor; if not, implement within 40 days, record compliance, and track the process fix through the management committee.
choices.outcome: Right. Under the BCO 1962 either side may appeal to the Governor within 30 days of the order. Findings must be implemented within 40 days, counted from the appeal decision if there is an appeal. The BC&FRF asks banks to have a control mechanism for implementing Mohtasib decisions.

choices.text: Ignore the finding, because the customer already received a full refund.
choices.outcome: An unappealed order becomes final. Failing to implement it can lead SBP to impose a fine or penalty, and the BC&FRF calls non-compliance a violation of section 82E(5) of the BCO.

choices.text: Pay the compensation, but leave the sales process unchanged, since only money was really at stake.
choices.outcome: Paying is part of compliance, but the finding also directed process improvements. Implementing only half a finding is not compliance.

choices.text: Ask the Mohtasib for a stay while the bank files a civil suit.
choices.outcome: The Mohtasib has no power to issue stay orders, and the route for a bank that disagrees is an appeal to the SBP Governor within 30 days.

cards.title: The Banking Mohtasib under the BCO 1962

cards.back: Part IVA of the Banking Companies Ordinance 1962 (sections 82A to 82G).
Banking malpractice, arbitrary or discriminatory action, breaches of banking laws or SBP directives, inordinate delay or inefficiency, and corruption or maladministration.
The customer first tells the bank in writing. If the bank does not respond, or responds unsatisfactorily, within 45 days, the customer may complain within a further 45 days.
It hears both sides, tries mediation, then may direct the bank to reconsider, change its decision, pay reasonable compensation or improve its functioning.
Order that a loan be given, issue stay orders, or take up matters pending before, or already decided by, a court or SBP.
Appeal to the SBP Governor within 30 days, decided within 60 days. The bank implements within 40 days.

items.label: Customer writes to the bank
items.detail: Written notice to the bank of the intention to complain.

items.label: Bank's window
items.detail: If there is no reply, or an unsatisfactory one, in this period, the customer may go to the Mohtasib.

items.label: Filing window
items.detail: Complaint filed within a further 45 days; the Mohtasib may condone a justified delay.

items.label: Appeal window
items.detail: Bank, bank official or complainant may appeal the order to the SBP Governor.

items.label: Implementation
items.detail: The bank implements the findings and reports compliance; counted from the appeal decision if appealed.

cards.title: Handling a walk-in complaint at a branch
cards.prompt: Put the branch steps in the order Pillar 5 expects.
steps: Listen and confirm what loss, inconvenience or distress the customer alleges
Log it in the CMS, even if you expect to fix it today
Give the tracking number by SMS and email and explain how to follow up
Resolve it, or escalate it within the bank's timelines
Send the final reply in writing, with reasons and the second forum if declined
Tag the root cause so complaint analysis can drive a fix

cards.question: A walk-in visitor with no account at Kohsar Bank complains that a pay order she bought at the counter was wrongly issued. What should the branch do?
options: Tell her to complain directly to the Banking Mohtasib
Refuse it, because only account holders may complain to the bank
Refer her to the bank that will receive the pay order
Accept and log the complaint, because services that need no account are covered
cards.explanation: Pillar 5 says consumers with no customer relationship must not be refused when complaining about a service for which a bank account is not required.

cards.title: Kohsar case: finding the hidden complaints
cards.body:
Mehwish's review of Multan Cantt found 27 complaints resolved at the counter but never logged.

**Why it matters.**
- Every complaint that fits the definition must be recorded and processed through the CMS, whatever the channel or outcome.
- At least one person in each branch must be responsible for logging every complaint reported there.
- Quarterly complaint returns to SBP's Consumer Protection Department are endorsed by the FTC owner and the head of compliance, so missing data is a reporting problem too.

**What the data showed once logged.** Eleven of the 27 were about the same thing: card renewal fees charged on dormant accounts, which Pillar 3 forbids until the account is reactivated.

**Fixes.** A system block on renewals for dormant accounts, refunds to affected customers, branch training on logging, and a monthly CMS-versus-register check by the area office.

cards.title: Call-centre rules that protect complainants
cards.body:
Pillar 5 sets clear standards for call centres:

- 'Card lost, stolen or block' is the first IVR option, with a wait of no more than one minute for those calls.
- Agents must never refuse to lodge a complaint.
- Callers are told calls are recorded; all calls are recorded and kept at least one year.
- Agents are trained on digital fraud, policies and complaint handling, and can block all of a customer's digital channels in one step with consent.
- Products are marketed only on toll-free numbers.

cards.title: Hearing Hall take-aways
items: A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction alleging loss, inconvenience or distress; never treat one as a service request.
Log every complaint in the CMS, including those from Sunwai, SBP and the Mohtasib and those fixed at the branch; records are kept permanently, except EFT complaints.
Tracking number by SMS and email; acknowledgement within 48 hours; minor in 3 or 7 working days; major with an interim reply and disposal within 15 days; fraud final reply within 30 days.
Declines are in writing, with reasons, evidence and the second forum's contact details; an Urdu complaint gets an Urdu reply.
Banking Mohtasib: 45 days for the bank to respond, a further 45 days to file, 30 days to appeal to the SBP Governor, 40 days to implement.
Complaint data drives fixes and is audited at least once a year.

cards.prompt: Recall a complaint you or your team handled informally. Would it have been logged, acknowledged and answered in writing under these rules? What would the data have told your managers?

quiz.question: Which of these is a complaint under the BC&FRF definition?
options: A question about the opening hours of a branch
A request for a duplicate statement for visa purposes
A request to replace a worn-out debit card
A verbal statement that a fee was wrongly charged, causing the customer a loss
quiz.explanation: A complaint is any written, digital or verbal expression of dissatisfaction alleging financial loss, inconvenience or distress from a product or service. Requests and enquiries without dissatisfaction are service requests.

quiz.question: A call-centre agent resolves a complaint on the call and gives the tracking number verbally. What is wrong?
options: The tracking number must be sent by SMS and email, not given through calls alone
The tracking number must be posted to the customer within 15 working days
Nothing, because the complaint was resolved on the first call
The agent should not have issued any tracking number for a complaint resolved on the call
quiz.explanation: Pillar 5 says every logged complaint gets a tracking number provided through SMS and email (if available), and that it must not be given through calls alone.

quiz.question: A complaint will clearly take more than 7 working days to investigate. How must the bank treat it?
options: As a minor complaint, with a final reply within 7 working days
As a major complaint, with an interim reply after 10 working days and disposal within 15 days
As a service request until the investigation finds fault
As a major complaint, with no interim reply needed as long as it is resolved within 45 working days
