quiz.explanation: Any complaint needing more than 7 working days is major. It needs an interim reply after 10 working days and must be disposed of within 15 days; fraud-related final replies are due within 30 days of lodging.

quiz.question: A customer disputes a credit card transaction made in Lahore. What does Pillar 5 say about the investigation?
options: The customer must pay the disputed amount before the bank investigates
It may not exceed 45 working days, and no mark-up is charged on the disputed amount meanwhile
It must finish within 7 working days because it is a minor complaint
It may take as long as the card scheme's rules need, with mark-up charged on the amount as normal
quiz.explanation: For disputes originating in Pakistan, resolution may not exceed 45 working days, and the bank may not charge mark-up during the investigation unless the dispute is settled in its favour.

quiz.question: Kohsar Bank declines a complaint after investigation. Which reply meets Pillar 5?
options: A written reply giving reasons and evidence, and the alternate forum with contact details
A phone call explaining the decision, followed by closure in the CMS
An SMS saying the complaint is closed, with the tracking number
A written reply saying the bank's decision is final and cannot be escalated to any other forum
quiz.explanation: When a complaint cannot be resolved in the customer's favour, the bank must say so in writing, give the reasons, justification or evidence, and name the alternate grievance forum and its contact details.

quiz.question: How long must a bank keep its record of complaints and their resolution, apart from electronic fund transfer complaints?
options: Until the next SBP inspection is completed
Ten years from account closure
Five years from the final reply
Permanently
quiz.explanation: Pillar 5 says complaint records are kept permanently, except electronic fund transfer complaints, which are kept for 5 years or longer under the bank's policy. Records under court or law enforcement action are kept until the case ends.

quiz.question: Under the BCO 1962, what must a customer do before complaining to the Banking Mohtasib?
options: Wait 90 days after the disputed transaction
Tell the bank in writing and allow it 45 days to reply
Obtain a court order showing the bank acted unlawfully
Lodge a complaint on SBP's Sunwai portal and wait for its decision
quiz.explanation: Section 82D requires the complainant to intimate the bank in writing first. If the bank fails to respond, or responds unsatisfactorily, within 45 days, the customer may file within a further 45 days.

quiz.question: Which order is outside the Banking Mohtasib's powers under the BCO 1962?
options: Directing the bank to improve its functioning
Directing the bank to grant a loan to the complainant
Directing the bank to reconsider its decision
Directing the bank to pay the complainant reasonable compensation
quiz.explanation: Section 82E lets the Mohtasib direct reconsideration, changes to decisions, reasonable compensation and improvements, but says in no case may it direct that loans, advances or finance be given.

quiz.question: The Mohtasib decides against Kohsar Bank, and the bank appeals to the SBP Governor, who upholds the finding. When must the bank implement it?
options: Within 40 days of the Governor's decision on the appeal
Within 60 days of the customer's first written complaint to the bank
Within 40 days of the Mohtasib's original order
Within 30 days of the Mohtasib's original order
quiz.explanation: Findings must be implemented within 40 days. When an appeal is made to the Governor, the 40 days run from the date of the appeal decision.

quiz.question: What must a branch do with a complaint it resolves at the counter within minutes?
options: Record it only in the branch's paper register
Log it in the CMS like any other complaint
Log it only if the customer asks for a tracking number
Treat it as a service request because it was resolved
quiz.explanation: All complaints that fit the definition must be recorded and processed through the CMS, regardless of channel and whether resolved at branch, region or head office.

sessions.title: Customer Data Secrecy, Training and Inspection Readiness
sessions.summary: Protect customer data under Pillar 4 and the BCO 1962 duty of fidelity and secrecy, respond to data breaches on time, then bring the whole framework together: the training policy and annual plan, customer awareness, reporting to SBP, internal audit and the records an SBP review will ask to see.
objectives: Apply the lawful bases, consent, confidentiality and third-party rules for customer data
Respond to a customer data breach within the BC&FRF's timelines
Describe the training and development policy, annual training plan and awareness duties under Pillar 6
Prepare evidence for internal audit and SBP: returns, records, audits and a recap of SBP's expectations

cards.title: A list on a phone
cards.setting: Conduct and FTC department, Islamabad. Friday, 4:15 pm.

lines.text: A customer sent us a screenshot. Someone called him, knew his card's last digits and his balance, and asked for an OTP 'to stop a fraud'.
My team found that an agency telemarketer photographed a customer list on his phone before he left the agency.
Then this is a data breach. We have to protect customers from further losses now, and tell affected customers within 48 hours what we are doing about it.
And next month the SBP inspection team visits. They'll ask about this, our training plan and our complaint data.
Final stage: the Vault and the Review. Lock down the data, then prove our whole conduct programme works.

scenes.heading: Secrecy is the law
scenes.narration: Section 33A of the Banking Companies Ordinance 1962 requires banks to keep customers' affairs secret, and every director, officer and employee makes a declaration of fidelity and secrecy before taking office. Pillar 4 of the BC&FRF builds on that duty.

scenes.heading: Lawful bases
scenes.narration: Processing is fair and lawful only if the customer has given verifiable consent, or it is needed for a contract with the customer, to meet a legal obligation, or to protect the customer's vital interests. Data is used only for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes.

scenes.heading: No selling or sharing
scenes.narration: Banks may not divulge, share or sell customer data. The exceptions are credit information sent to eCIB or an approved credit bureau, and outsourcing partners bound by confidentiality clauses.

scenes.heading: Need to know
scenes.narration: Staff see customer data only on a need-to-know basis, with access logged and monitored. Call agents see only the last four digits of card numbers, and nobody may ask a customer to say an OTP aloud.

scenes.heading: Keep it only as long as needed
scenes.narration: Data is kept accurate and up to date, held no longer than its purpose or the law requires, and then destroyed or permanently deleted. Customers may withdraw consent at any time.

items.label: Collect
items.detail: Only what a specified purpose needs, on a lawful basis, transparently.

items.label: Use
items.detail: For that purpose only; not for marketing unless the customer opted in.

items.label: Protect
items.detail: Encryption, masking, need-to-know access, logs and access reviews.

items.label: Share
items.detail: Only with consent or legal compulsion, eCIB or bureaus, or bound outsourcing partners.

items.label: Retain and destroy
items.detail: No longer than needed, then destroyed or permanently deleted.

cards.title: Share it or keep it?
cards.prompt: Decide whether each disclosure of customer data is permitted under Pillar 4.

items.text: Reporting a borrower's credit information to eCIB
Selling a list of high-balance customers to a property developer
Giving statements to a printing vendor under contract, supervised by bank staff
Telling a customer's brother his balance because he 'is family'
Disclosing information because a law or court order compels it
Using customers' phone numbers for marketing after they opted out
Letting a vendor use bank customer data for its own commercial offers
Sharing data with a customer's written consent for a stated purpose

cards.question: Customer data was compromised in a breach, and some customers lost money. What does Pillar 4 require?
options: Inform customers within 30 days, after SBP has reviewed the incident
Inform affected customers within 48 hours of the steps taken, and compensate financial losses within two business days
Inform only SBP, so that customers are not alarmed
Compensate customers only if a court finds the bank negligent
cards.explanation: Pillar 4 requires immediate steps to protect customers from further losses, informing them within 48 hours about the steps being taken, and compensating financial losses from such incidents within two business days. Frauds and breaches must also be reported to SBP within the stipulated time.

cards.title: Pillar 6: training that SBP expects to see
cards.body:
**Training and development policy**
- Builds a culture of responsible conduct and FTC; standalone or a distinct part of the bank's wider training policy.
- With SOPs covering scope, training needs assessment, budget, mandatory training man-days, and how initiatives are assessed and monitored.

**Annual training plan**
- Training is ongoing, with regular updates and refresher courses.
- Distinct programmes for new hires and for existing staff, and stated requirements for third-party employees.
- Sessions on new SBP instructions; local and global developments in FTC and financial fraud, especially digital fraud; and SECP's training requirements for selling third-party products.
- Modules cover the code of conduct and possible discipline for mis-selling, fraud and similar breaches.

**PWD capacity building**
- Mandatory awareness and practical training for branch staff on serving persons with disabilities; all employees know the inclusion policy.

**Effectiveness**
- Systems to monitor quality and impact, and assessment tools that check real learning.

items.label: Complaint returns to SBP
items.detail: Within 15 working days of quarter end, endorsed by the FTC owner and the head of compliance.

items.label: Training and awareness data
items.detail: Sent to SBP's BPRD by the 15th of the month after each half-year.

items.label: PWD policy progress
items.detail: Detailed progress report on the PWD policy to the board every half-year.

items.label: Complaint mechanism audit
items.detail: Internal audit reviews complaint handling at least yearly and reports deviations to the board.

items.label: Satisfaction survey
items.detail: Survey of complainants' satisfaction at least once in two years, sent to SBP's CPD.

items.label: Complaint disclosure
items.detail: Commentary on complaint handling, total complaints and average resolution time.

lines.text: The agency says the telemarketer was theirs, not ours. Surely that's their breach?
Outsourcing never removes our primary responsibility for the security and confidentiality of customer data. Third-party staff shouldn't sit where data can be compromised in the first place.
The calls asked for OTPs. We'd better remind everyone, and every customer, that we never ask for OTPs.
What do we do first? Customers are getting calls right now.

cards.title: Containing the breach
cards.situation: It is Friday night. About 600 customers are on the leaked list; four have reported losses after sharing OTPs with callers who claimed to be from Kohsar Bank. The agency contract has a confidentiality clause. The CEO wants to 'wait until Monday to understand the full picture'.

choices.text: Act now: alert customers and offer channel blocks, tell them within 48 hours what is being done, compensate losses within two business days, report to SBP on time, enforce the contract.
choices.outcome: Right. Pillar 4 requires immediate protective steps, customer communication within 48 hours, compensation within two business days, and timely reporting to SBP, with staff held accountable for delays. The bank keeps primary responsibility despite outsourcing.

choices.text: Wait until Monday as the CEO suggests, then decide on a single public statement.
choices.outcome: Delay lets the fraud continue. The framework makes the bank liable for losses caused by delays in taking remedial measures, such as blocking channels, and sets a 48-hour window for informing customers.

choices.text: Compensate the four customers who reported losses, but tell the others nothing to avoid panic.
choices.outcome: Compensating is right, but the other 594 customers are exposed. They must be told what the bank is doing to protect them.

choices.text: Ask the agency to handle customer communication, since its employee caused the leak.
choices.outcome: Outsourcing does not absolve the bank of its responsibility for data confidentiality. The bank must lead the response and communicate with its own customers.

cards.title: Evidence for the SBP review
cards.prompt: Match each item an inspector may request to the requirement it proves.

pairs.right: The board approved the bank's internal FTC framework and policies
The management committee met at least twice a year and tracked decisions
Ongoing, refresher and induction training, third-party staff included
Complaint data reported to SBP's CPD on time and endorsed
Reasons documented for any fee increase of 25 percent or more
BC&FRF implementation, KFS accuracy and complaint handling were tested

cards.back: Banks must never require customers to give OTPs verbally to any officer, call-centre agents included.
Call agents see only the last four digits of credit and debit card numbers.
When an employee or third-party worker changes role, IT access no longer needed is withdrawn immediately.
Not placed in decision-making roles or where customer data could be compromised.
Customers' biometric data is never stored or transmitted unencrypted.
Personal information is not used for marketing unless the customer opted in, and opt-outs are actioned promptly.

cards.title: Responding to a customer data breach
cards.prompt: Put the response steps in a sensible order.
steps: Contain the leak and help customers block exposed channels
Identify the affected customers and the data involved
Inform affected customers within 48 hours of the steps being taken
Compensate customers' financial losses within two business days
Report to SBP within the stipulated time and fix accountability for any delay
Fix the root cause and review third-party access and contracts

cards.question: Which statement about Pillar 6's annual training plan is correct?
options: It needs distinct programmes for new hires and existing staff, refreshers, and stated requirements for third-party staff
It needs one induction course per employee, after which refreshers are optional
It covers only customer-facing staff, because conduct risk arises at the counter
It is optional for banks that already run AML/CFT training each year
cards.explanation: Pillar 6 requires an annual plan under the training policy, with ongoing training, regular updates and refreshers, distinct programmes for newly hired and existing employees, and training requirements for third-party staff.

cards.title: Kohsar case: the mock inspection
cards.body:
Two weeks before SBP's visit, Zara's team ran a mock review.

**Found and fixed:**
- **Training:** no needs assessment and no third-party module. **Fix:** needs assessment run, agency staff added to the plan, short tests after each module.
- **Complaints:** 27 unlogged branch complaints. **Fix:** logged, root causes tagged, monthly checks by area offices.
- **Fees:** a 30 percent cheque book fee rise with no written reasons. **Fix:** justification documented for inspectors, as required for increases of 25 percent or more.
- **Breach:** customers informed within 48 hours, losses compensated, SBP informed, agency contract terms enforced.
- **PWD:** ramp built at Multan Cantt; sign-language awareness training booked for at least one person in each model branch.

**Lesson:** inspectors look for evidence that the framework works in practice, not only for policies on paper.

cards.title: Raise customer awareness too
Vault and Review take-aways
items: BCO 1962 section 33A demands fidelity and secrecy; Pillar 4 requires lawful bases, purpose limits, need-to-know access and no selling or sharing of customer data.
Never ask for OTPs verbally; mask card numbers for call agents; outsourcing never removes the bank's responsibility for data.
After a breach: protect customers at once, inform them within 48 hours, compensate losses within two business days and report to SBP in time.
Pillar 6 needs a training policy and an annual plan with refreshers, separate new-hire and existing-staff programmes, third-party staff and PWD training.
SBP receives quarterly complaint returns and bi-annual training and awareness data; internal audit tests the BC&FRF, the KFS and complaint handling.
Inspectors want evidence of fair outcomes, not only policies.

cards.prompt: If an SBP inspector stopped you tomorrow and asked how your role delivers fair treatment of customers, what two pieces of evidence would you show, and what gap would you want fixed first?

quiz.question: Which is one of the lawful bases for processing customer data listed in Pillar 4?
options: Processing that an outsourcing vendor requests for its own analytics and product research
Processing that would help the bank market new products
Processing that a staff member considers useful in the future
Processing needed to comply with a legal obligation that applies to the bank
quiz.explanation: Pillar 4 lists verifiable consent, or necessity for a contract with the customer, a legal obligation on the bank, or the customer's vital interests. Marketing convenience is not a lawful basis on its own.

quiz.question: A relationship manager wants to send a customer list to a partner company for its own marketing. What does Pillar 4 say?
options: It is allowed once the list is approved by the branch manager
It is not allowed: customer data may not be divulged, shared or sold outside narrow exceptions
It is allowed for customers who have not complained in the past year
It is allowed, as long as the partner company first signs a non-disclosure agreement with the bank
quiz.explanation: Banks shall not divulge, share or sell customer data to anybody. The exceptions are credit information to eCIB or an approved bureau and companies with outsourcing data-sharing agreements that enforce confidentiality. A partner's own marketing is not one of them.

quiz.question: What does section 33A of the Banking Companies Ordinance 1962 require of every bank officer and employee?
options: A declaration of fidelity and secrecy before entering office
A personal guarantee for any data breach in their unit
Registration with SBP as an approved data handler
An annual written test on data protection rules
quiz.explanation: Section 33A requires banks to keep customers' affairs secret and requires directors, auditors, advisers, officers and other employees to make a declaration of fidelity and secrecy before taking office.

quiz.question: A call-centre agent asks a caller to read out the OTP he just received 'to verify the account'. What is the problem?
options: Nothing, if the customer called from the registered number
Nothing, if the call is recorded and kept for one year
Only that the agent should have asked for the PIN instead
Banks must never require customers to give OTPs verbally to their officers or agents
quiz.explanation: Pillar 4 says banks shall not require customers to provide OTPs verbally to their officers, call-centre agents included. Asking for a PIN is even worse.

quiz.question: After a data breach in which some customers lost money, by when must Kohsar Bank compensate them?
options: Within 45 working days, as for card disputes
Within 15 working days, after the complaint is investigated
Within two business days
After SBP confirms the amount of each loss
quiz.explanation: Pillar 4 says that where customers suffer a financial loss from a data security breach, the bank compensates them within two business days, and informs them within 48 hours of the steps being taken.

quiz.question: An outsourcing vendor leaks customer data. Which statement reflects Pillar 4?
options: The vendor alone is responsible, because the outsourcing contract contains a confidentiality clause
Outsourcing never removes the bank's primary responsibility for data confidentiality
The bank is responsible only if its own staff caused the breach
Responsibility passes to SBP once the bank reports the breach
quiz.explanation: Outsourcing any activity does not absolve the bank of its primary responsibility for the security, integrity and confidentiality of data. Contracts must allow termination for breaches, and vendors must report breaches immediately.

quiz.question: Which item must Pillar 6's annual training plan include?
options: A single course that replaces all refresher training
A ban on online learning for conduct topics
Training on SECP's requirements for selling third-party products
Training limited to employees in grades above officer level, who supervise others
quiz.explanation: The plan must include sessions on new SBP instructions, developments in FTC and financial fraud, especially digital fraud, and SECP's training requirements for selling third-party products, with modules on the code of conduct and discipline.

quiz.question: How often must banks send data on training, capacity building and consumer awareness measures to SBP?
options: Only when SBP's inspection team asks for it
Annually, with the audited financial statements
Monthly, within 10 days of the end of each month
Bi-annually, by the 15th of the month following each half-year
quiz.explanation: Section 6.3 requires bi-annual data on training, capacity building and consumer awareness measures to be sent to SBP's BPRD by the 15th of the month following each half-year, in the Annexure-6A format.

quiz.question: How often must internal audit review the bank's complaint handling mechanism?
options: At least annually, with deviations reported to the board
Every quarter, replacing the quarterly returns to SBP
Once every three years, during the full branch audit cycle
Only when SBP raises a finding on complaints
quiz.explanation: Pillar 5 makes the internal complaint handling mechanism subject to internal audit at least annually, with deviations and non-compliance recorded and reported to the board.

quiz.question: Kohsar Bank raises a service fee by 25 percent. What must it keep for SBP's inspection team?
options: Nothing, as long as the new fee is in the schedule of charges
A board resolution approving each individual customer's charge
Written consent from every affected customer before the change
Documented reasons and justification for the increase
quiz.explanation: Pillar 3 requires banks to document the reasons for any fee increase of 25 percent or more and make them available to the SBP inspection team, alongside the general rule that charges be reasonable and empirically based.

bank.question: An EMI argues that every pillar of the BC&FRF applies to it exactly as to a bank. Which reply is accurate?
options: EMIs are fully exempt until SBP issues a separate EMI framework
Several sections, Pillar 6 among them, are not mandatory for EMIs but are encouraged
Only Pillar 1 applies to EMIs; the rest is for banks and DFIs
EMIs follow exactly the same rules as banks, but only for customers who hold their cards
bank.explanation: The framework applies proportionately: sections such as 3.2.4(5), 3.2.5, 3.3, 4.5, 5.3 and Pillar 6 are not made mandatory for EMIs, though they are encouraged to follow them. The rest applies according to their business.

bank.question: A bank's head of retail says the FTC principles in Part One are 'aspirations' and only Part Two is enforceable. Which response is correct?
options: He is right for corporate clients, but wrong where retail customers are concerned
Part One becomes binding only after the bank's board adopts it
Part One's principles are expressly described as obligations for institutions
He is right; Part One is a preamble with no regulatory force
bank.explanation: The introduction describes Part One's FTC outcome-based principles as obligations for financial institutions, and Part One asks institutions to take all appropriate measures to achieve those outcomes.

bank.question: Kohsar Bank prices a new debit card replacement fee by copying the highest fee in the market without any cost study. Which principle is most at risk?
options: Principle E, which requires products suited to affordability
Principle A, which bars market manipulation and collusion
Principle F, on reasonable, empirically based charges
Principle D, which protects customers from discrimination
bank.explanation: Principle F expects charges that match the service, are comparable to what other banks charge and have some empirical analysis behind them. Copying the highest fee without analysis fails that test.

bank.question: Two banks agree privately to set the same high charge for cash deposit slips at their counters. Which principle and rule does this most clearly breach?
options: Principle B's disclosure duty, because the new charge was never advertised to customers
Principle A and Pillar 3's ban on colluding to fix terms against consumers
Principle H's dispute duty, because customers cannot complain
Principle G's data duty, because customer data was shared
bank.explanation: Principle A calls for avoiding collusive practices, and Pillar 3's sales practices forbid colluding to fix features or terms to the detriment of consumers. It also clashes with the ban on charges for cash handling at counters.

bank.question: Which of these does Pillar 1 assign to the management committee for conduct and FTC?
options: Setting an escalation policy for conduct-related non-compliance
Approving the bank's internal FTC framework on the board's behalf
Conducting the annual internal audit of complaint handling
Appointing the members of the board risk management committee
bank.explanation: The management committee must develop and implement a policy on the escalation hierarchy for conduct-related non-compliance. Board committees, framework approval and the internal audit belong to the board and to internal audit.

bank.question: What does the BC&FRF say about the 2016 Conduct Assessment Framework (BC&CPD Circular No. 3 of 2016)?
options: The management committee must ensure it is implemented, as amended
It is withdrawn and replaced entirely by the BC&FRF
It applies only to microfinance banks and EMIs
It is optional guidance for banks that want to run a voluntary self-assessment
bank.explanation: Pillar 1 lists, among the management committee's minimum functions, ensuring implementation of the Conduct Assessment Framework under BC&CPD Circular No. 3 of 2016 as amended. The BC&FRF keeps it in force rather than replacing it.

bank.question: A board committee member asks what powers the conduct oversight committee needs under Pillar 1. Which answer is accurate?
options: Power to set individual sales targets for each branch
A mandate to seek information from management on conduct compliance and service benchmarks
Authority to handle customer complaints directly, in place of the bank's complaints unit and call centre
Authority to approve every new product before management sees it
bank.explanation: The dedicated committee, or the BRMC with an expanded role, must at least have the mandate to seek information from management on compliance with conduct and FTC rules, internal policies and service quality benchmarks, and stay informed of best practice.

bank.question: Which statement about the management committee's membership and reporting is consistent with Pillar 1?
options: It consists only of the compliance team and reports to the CEO when needed
It is chaired by the external auditor and reports once a year to shareholders at the annual general meeting
It consists only of independent directors and reports to SBP every quarter
Group heads of business and control functions; reports at least twice a year to the board committee
bank.explanation: Pillar 1 says the committee includes group heads of relevant business units and control functions, meets at least bi-annually and presents at least bi-annual performance reports to the BRMC or dedicated board committee.

bank.question: Who must assess the status of implementation of the BC&FRF and related policies inside a bank?
options: The head of sales
Internal audit
The Banking Mohtasib
The external auditor
bank.explanation: Section 1.4 gives internal audit the duty to assess implementation of the BC&FRF and related internal and regulatory instructions. Internal audit also checks KFS accuracy and audits complaint handling.

bank.question: A bank adds a new monthly SMS alert charge for all accounts. Which combination of steps meets Pillar 2 and Pillar 3?
options: Publish the new charge on the website on the day it starts
Add it to the next statement and treat payment as agreement
Notify each customer at least 30 days ahead through an agreed mode, display the change, and let customers exit or opt out without penalty
Inform customers by SMS within a week after the first deduction
bank.explanation: Changes to charges need at least 30 days' notice through a verifiably agreed mode plus display in branches and online. Customers may exit without penalty within the notice period, and subscription services carry a free look-up.

bank.question: What must accompany the facility offer letter for a term loan under Pillar 2?
options: A complete amortisation schedule showing principal and mark-up over the life of the loan or to the next re-pricing
A copy of the borrower's credit bureau report
A list of the bank's other financing products
A summary of the bank's annual financial statements
bank.explanation: Pillar 2 requires a complete amortisation schedule with the offer letter, showing the breakdown of principal and mark-up for the life of the loan or until the next re-pricing date, with a new schedule when floating rates reset.

bank.question: A loan has a guarantor. Which disclosure duty does Pillar 2 place on the bank?
options: Send the guarantor a copy only if the borrower defaults
Inform the guarantor verbally at the signing ceremony
Let the borrower decide what the guarantor is told
Inform the guarantor of rights, obligations and default consequences, provide the contracts and the KFS, and keep the acknowledgement
bank.explanation: Pillar 2 tells banks to inform guarantors of their rights and obligations and of the implications of the borrower's default, to give them the credit and security contracts and the product KFS, and to retain the acknowledgement.

bank.question: A bank wants to launch a new credit card. What must it give prospective customers before issue, and what must it keep?
options: The annual fee schedule, signed by the branch manager only
The full terms only after the card is activated
A brochure with sample rewards, kept on the website
An upfront Summary Box, and a duplicate signed by the customer and an authorised banker
bank.explanation: Banks must provide a Summary Box as an upfront key fact sheet for credit cards and, before issuing any card, keep a duplicate signed by the customer and an authorised banker.

bank.question: Kohsar Bank's telesales team calls a customer, describes a card protection plan, takes her 'yes' and activates it during the same call. Which rule is broken?
options: Products may be sold only by staff on the bank's payroll
Telesales calls must last at least fifteen minutes
The customer must visit a branch in person to buy any card protection plan
Products may not be offered, marketed and sold on a single call
bank.explanation: Pillar 2 tells marketing personnel not to offer, market and sell products on a single call, and Pillar 3 forbids marketing and closing the sale of third-party products on the same call.

bank.question: A bank sells a third-party investment product under its own brand without saying it acts as an agent. What is the issue?
options: The issue is only the font size used on the brochure
Third-party products must be marketed with an explicit statement that the bank acts as agent or distributor
Third-party products may not be sold by banks at all
Only the provider's name may appear on any document
bank.explanation: Pillar 3 forbids marketing and selling third-party products under the bank's name without explicitly saying the product is sold as agent or distributor, and the basic fact sheet must carry a distributor disclaimer.

bank.question: What does the central control function for third-party product sales do, and what is the key condition on it?
options: It verifies sales proposals and has no incentive linked to those sales
It handles complaints about these products, and it is staffed by the provider's own agents
It sets sales targets, and it reports to the insurance company
It designs the products, and it shares commission with branches
bank.explanation: Banks offering third-party products must have a centralised, independent control function to verify information in sales proposals, and it may not have any incentive linked to the sale of these products.

bank.question: What must the management committee's quarterly MIS on third-party product sales include at a minimum?
options: Persistency, cancellations, alleged and proven mis-selling complaints, adverse audit findings and SLA breaches
Premium income and the insurer's share price performance
Only the number of policies sold compared with target
Sales volumes by branch and the top ten sellers' commissions
bank.explanation: Pillar 3 requires quarterly review of third-party product sales, with MIS that at least covers persistency, cancellations, alleged and proven mis-selling complaints, adverse internal audit observations and SLA breaches.

bank.question: How long must a bank keep call-back confirmation recordings for bancassurance sales?
options: One year from the date of sale, as for other inbound and outbound call-centre recordings
Two months, as for CCTV footage
At least 7 years or until the product matures, whichever is later
Until the free look-up period ends
bank.explanation: Pillar 3 requires CBC records for third-party products for at least 7 years or the maturity of the product, whichever is later. The one-year rule applies to ordinary call-centre recordings.

bank.question: A salaried customer's car loan instalment falls due five days before his salary is credited each month, and he often pays late. What does Pillar 3 expect?
options: Require a guarantor before accepting any further instalments from him
Charge late fees, because the contract date is binding
Fix the billing cycle so the due date suits his salary date
Report him to eCIB after the second late payment
bank.explanation: Pillar 3 asks banks to fix billing cycles for consumer financing in a way that makes timely repayment convenient, for example aligning a salaried person's due date with salary disbursement.

bank.question: A customer pays the entire outstanding balance of her loan, but the system parks it against future instalments. What does Pillar 3 require?
options: Parking is correct if the contract does not mention early settlement
Controls that apply payments as the customer intended, settling the loan rather than parking the money
Parking is correct until the customer submits a formal early-settlement form
The bank may choose the treatment that earns the most mark-up
bank.explanation: Banks must have effective controls so payments are accounted as the customer intended even if SOPs were not followed; a full payment is appropriated as settlement rather than parked for future instalments.

bank.question: A bank's recovery team plans to repossess a leased vehicle after default. Which step is required?
options: A same-day call to the borrower's employer to locate the vehicle
Immediate repossession, because the lease agreement allows it
A notice published in the newspaper, with no separate letter
A 14-day duly acknowledged notice first, and a chance for the borrower to remove belongings from the vehicle
bank.explanation: The 14-day acknowledged notice applies before repossessing a leased vehicle, and the borrower must be allowed to take possession of valuables or goods in the vehicle first.

bank.question: A collection agency charges a borrower Rs 15,000 for repossession costs that actually cost Rs 9,000. What does Pillar 3 say?
options: The bank may recover double costs where the borrower defaulted twice
Only the actual cost of third-party services such as repossession may be recovered
Any amount is allowed if disclosed in the schedule of charges
The agency may add a fair margin on top of its costs, as long as the contract allows it
bank.explanation: Banks may recover only the actual charges or cost incurred for third-party services such as vehicle repossession, valuation or credit reports, and Pillar 3's sales practices also forbid charging more than actual cost.

bank.question: Before signing up a co-debtor on a financing facility, what must the bank do?
options: Register the co-debtor with eCIB before the facility is approved
Obtain the co-debtor's salary slip only, since liability is shared equally
Rely on the primary borrower to explain the terms to the co-debtor
Verify identity and relationship, and take reasonable steps to ensure the co-debtor understands liability for the full debt
bank.explanation: Pillar 3 requires verifying the co-debtor's identity and relation to the primary customer, and taking reasonable steps so the co-debtor understands liability for the full amount and their rights under the agreement.

bank.question: What must a bank's PWD policy framework and strategy cover at a minimum?
options: Only physical ramps, since other measures are voluntary
Only digital accessibility, since branches are being phased out
Accessibility infrastructure, accessibility audits, accessible products and services, and employment and career development of PWDs
Only staff recruitment quotas, since customers are covered elsewhere
bank.explanation: Section 3.3.1 requires a board-approved policy and strategy covering accessibility infrastructure, accessibility audits of premises, accessible products and services, and the employment, retention and career development of PWDs.

bank.question: A branch opens an account for an illiterate blind customer. What do the BC&FRF's visually impaired guidelines require?
options: The account may only be used for cash deposits
The account may only be opened jointly with a sighted relative
The manager reads out the terms in the presence of a witness known to the customer before signing
The customer must appoint a power of attorney before the account opens
bank.explanation: Annexure 3B says the branch manager or operations manager reads out the terms in the presence of a witness known to an illiterate visually impaired customer before the forms are signed. Joint accounts and attorneys are options, not conditions.

bank.question: Which statement about financing for visually impaired applicants is correct under Annexure 3B?
options: The bank applies the same procedure and criteria as for other applicants, with no extra conditions beyond standard ones
The bank must refer each application to SBP for approval
The bank must require a sighted guarantor for every loan
The bank may cap loan amounts at a lower limit for safety
bank.explanation: Annexure 3B requires the same procedure and criteria as for other applicants and forbids additional terms beyond requisite standard conditions.

bank.question: Kohsar Bank receives a complaint written in Urdu. In what language must it reply?
options: Whichever language the complaint handler prefers
English, as the bank's official language
Both languages, with English taking precedence
Urdu
bank.explanation: Pillar 5 says that when a complaint is lodged in Urdu, banks respond in the same language.

bank.question: A bank delays a refund owed to a complainant for two months beyond the resolution date. What does Pillar 5 require beyond the refund?
options: Adequate compensation for the period of delay
A report to the Banking Mohtasib before paying
An apology letter signed by the CEO, but no money
Nothing, provided the refund is eventually paid in full
bank.explanation: Pillar 5 says institutions must adequately compensate customers for the period of delay in providing relief, and must escalate complaints that are not resolved in time.

bank.question: A complaints officer reclassifies a 'mis-selling' complaint as 'service quality' in the CMS so the mis-selling figures look better. What does Pillar 5 expect?
options: Category changes are allowed only with caution and review by a senior officer, and categories must map to SBP's
Categories may be changed only by the external auditor
Officers may reclassify freely, since categories are internal
Reclassification is fine if the customer is not told
bank.explanation: The SBP categories are the minimum and internal categories must map to them. Changes in category may be allowed with caution so that a senior officer can review them and take corrective action.

bank.question: Who must review and endorse the quarterly complaint returns before they go to SBP's Consumer Protection Department?
options: The chairman of the board and the company secretary
The bank's FTC owner and its head of compliance
The branch managers whose branches received complaints
The Banking Mohtasib and the bank's external auditor
bank.explanation: Quarterly returns on complaint handling are submitted after review and endorsement by the FTC owner and the head of compliance, within fifteen working days after quarter end.

bank.question: A customer complains that the bank refused to open an account for him because he is a politician. Which special mechanism applies?
options: There is no special route; PEP complaints follow the normal minor timeline
Only the Banking Mohtasib can hear complaints from politicians
The complaint must go to the board before anyone replies
The bank's senior focal person for PEPs handles it, and the PEP may go to SBP's focal person if unresolved after 15 working days
bank.explanation: Section 5.2 requires a senior-level focal person for PEP complaints about discrimination. If the grievance is not resolved within 15 working days, or the PEP is dissatisfied, he may contact the focal person appointed by SBP.

bank.question: Which matter falls outside what the Banking Mohtasib may take up under the BCO 1962?
options: A dispute already pending before a court
Fraudulent or unauthorised debits to an account
Delays in transferring funds or collecting a cheque
Complaints about remittances to or from abroad
bank.explanation: Section 82D(4) bars the Mohtasib from entertaining complaints while the matter is pending before a court or other legal forum. Unauthorised debits, delayed transfers and remittances are expressly within jurisdiction.

bank.question: Kohsar Bank's complaint was rejected by the Mohtasib, and the customer is still unhappy. What does section 82E say about the customer's options?
options: The customer must first complain on SBP's Sunwai portal and obtain its permission before suing
The customer must accept the decision, which ends all legal remedies
Nothing in Part IVA prevents the complainant from filing a suit against the bank
The customer may re-file with the Mohtasib after 45 days
bank.explanation: Section 82E(7) says nothing prevents a complainant from filing a suit against a bank if the complaint is rejected. The customer may also appeal to the SBP Governor within 30 days of the order.

bank.question: What does Pillar 5 say about mystery shopping and customer satisfaction surveys on complaint handling?
options: Mystery shopping is encouraged at least once in two years; satisfaction surveys are required at least once in two years and reported to SBP and the board
Both are required monthly and must be published on the website
Only mystery shopping is required, and only for digital banks
Both are optional and need not be reported anywhere
bank.explanation: Banks are encouraged to use mystery shopping of complaint handling at least once in two years. Satisfaction surveys on grievance handling must be held at least once in two years, sent to SBP's CPD and reported to the board.

bank.question: An employee moves from the call centre to the HR department. What does Pillar 4 require about her system access?
options: She keeps all old access for six months in case she is needed back
Her old access is withdrawn only if she requests it
Access she no longer needs is withdrawn immediately, and access rights are reviewed regularly
Her access is reviewed at the next annual audit
bank.explanation: Pillar 4 says IT access rights no longer required after a change in role are withdrawn immediately, new rights are assigned through an approved process, and regular reviews look for anomalies.

bank.question: A customer withdraws consent for the bank to process his data for a loyalty programme. What is the effect under Pillar 4?
options: The bank must immediately delete every record it holds about the customer, including account records
Withdrawal has no effect until the next account review
All processing before the withdrawal becomes unlawful
Processing on that consent must stop, but processing done before withdrawal remains lawful
bank.explanation: Customers may withdraw consent at any time through an agreed mode; withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before it. Records the bank must keep by law are not affected.

bank.question: Kohsar Bank uses a vendor to print and post customer statements. Which condition does Pillar 4 attach?
options: Customers must each sign consent before any statement is posted
The vendor must be licensed by SBP as a bank
The bank's own employee must supervise the whole process
The vendor may print statements only for accounts above a set balance
bank.explanation: Banks may use third parties for printing, stuffing and delivery of statements provided the bank's own employee supervises the entire process. Third-party staff may not be placed where customer data can be compromised.

bank.question: What must the training and development policy under Pillar 6 cover, with its SOPs?
options: Only the list of courses offered in the current year
Only the employees exempt from conduct training
Only the names of trainers and their qualifications
Scope, training needs assessment, training budget, mandatory training man-days, and assessment and monitoring of initiatives
bank.explanation: Pillar 6 says the policy and SOPs cover broad parameters such as scope, the training needs assessment process, budget, mandatory training man-days, and how initiatives are assessed and monitored.

bank.question: Which group does Pillar 6 single out for mandatory awareness and practical training on serving persons with disabilities?
options: Branch staff, while all employees must know the bank's PWD inclusion policy
HR staff only, since they recruit PWD employees
Board members only, since they approve the PWD policy
Call-centre staff only, since they take most phone requests from customers with disabilities
bank.explanation: Pillar 6 requires mandatory awareness, sensitisation and practical training for branch staff on serving PWDs, and requires all employees to be aware of the inclusion policy.

bank.question: Call-centre staff training is singled out in Pillar 5. Which requirement goes with it?
options: Training only for supervisors, who then brief agents
Training on digital fraud, policies and complaint handling, with an impact assessment of the training
Training delivered by the card schemes only
Training once at induction, with no later updates
bank.explanation: Pillar 5 says call centres must be adequately staffed and trained, particularly on digital fraud management, policies and query and complaint handling, and that banks assess the impact of the training.

bank.question: What must banks disclose in their annual accounts about complaint handling?
options: Nothing; complaint data goes only to SBP
A brief commentary on the complaint mechanism and initiatives, total complaints received and average resolution time
Only the number of complaints upheld by the Banking Mohtasib
The names of customers who complained during the year
bank.explanation: Pillar 5 requires a commentary on the internal complaint mechanism and the year's initiatives, plus the total complaints received directly and the average time taken to resolve them.

bank.question: An SBP inspector asks how Kohsar Bank knows its conduct training works. Which evidence best answers the Pillar 6 requirement?
options: The training budget approved by the board
Monitoring of training quality and impact, and assessment tools that check participation and learning
The number of hours each trainer delivered
A signed attendance register showing everyone attended
bank.explanation: Pillar 6 requires robust systems to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness and quality of training and capacity building, and assessment tools that ensure active participation, engagement and learning. Attendance alone does not show effectiveness.
